references.text: The Acts of the Apostles gives a more detailed account of Jesus' ascension, where the disciples see him being lifted up and a cloud takes him from their sight ([ref:Acts 1:9-11|Acts of the Apostles 1:9-11]). This is the parallel account to Luke's conclusion in his Gospel.

Mark's conclusion also tells of Jesus' ascension: "The Lord Jesus was taken up into heaven and sat down at God's right hand" ([ref:Mark 16:19|Mark 16:19]). Both texts describe the end of Jesus' earthly ministry.
Elijah was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind while Elisha watched ([ref:2 Kings 2:11|2 Kings 2:11]). This Old Testament ascension is a typological precursor to Jesus' ascension.
"God goes up amid shouts of joy, the Lord goes up with trumpet blast" ([ref:Psalm 47:6|Psalms 47:6]). In early Christian tradition, this psalm was understood as a prophecy about Christ's ascension.
"You have gone up on high" ([ref:Psalm 68:19|Psalms 68:19]) was interpreted messianically and linked to Christ's ascension, as Paul also does in Ephesians 4:8.
Paul quotes Psalm 68:19 and applies it to Christ who went up above all the heavens ([ref:Ephesians 4:8-10|Ephesians 4:8-10]). This confirms that Jesus' ascension fulfills Old Testament prophecy.
Christ entered heaven itself to appear before God's face on our behalf ([ref:Hebrews 9:24|Hebrews 9:24]). The ascension is the precondition for Jesus' ministry as our high priest in heaven.

The mystery of godliness includes that Christ "was taken up in glory" ([ref:1 Timothy 3:16|1 Timothy 3:16]). This is an early confession that summarizes Christ's work of salvation, including his ascension.

Jesus Christ "has gone into heaven and is at God's right hand" ([ref:1 Peter 3:22|1 Peter 3:22]). Peter's letter confirms that the ascension resulted in angels, authorities, and powers being subjected to Christ.

Just before the ascension, Jesus blessed his disciples by lifting up his hands ([ref:Luke 24:50|Luke 24:50]). The blessing and the ascension are closely connected – Jesus parted from them while he was still blessing them.
